metadata.summary: Nico de Boinville was given security support at Plumpton on Monday after a threat against the jockey was received and passed on to authorities.
metadata.content: Nico de Boinville 'escorted to his vehicle' and given security support after threat received | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Nico de Boinville 'escorted to his vehicle' and given security support after threat received Top jockey Nico de Boinville was racing at Plumpton and finished fifth in the opening race of the afternoon, before finishing third on his only other ride; he was given additional security protection throughout the day after a threat had been made to Nicky Henderson's yard Tuesday 17 November 2026 19:16, UK Image: Nico de Boinville was given additional security at Plumpton on Monday Nico de Boinville was given security support at Plumpton on Monday after a threat against the jockey was received and passed on to authorities. The multiple Grade One-wining jockey finished fifth aboard even-money favourite Ginolo for his boss Nicky Henderson in the opening race of the afternoon at the East Sussex track, after which he was informed he would be provided with extra security after officials became aware of the situation. De Boinville went on to finish third on his only other ride, the Henderson-trained Ionian in a handicap chase, the third race on the card. Explaining the sequence of events, Plumpton's clerk of the course Marcus Waters said: "We got a phone call from a person representing the PJA (Professional Jockeys Association) and the NTF (National Trainers Federation) regarding a threat that had gone in to the Henderson yard. metadata.summary: Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated suicide.
metadata.content: Wayne Rooney says he contemplated suicide during ‘lowest point’ of Manchester United career | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Wayne Rooney says he contemplated suicide during ‘lowest point’ of Manchester United career Wayne Rooney has revealed he considered taking his own life while playing for Manchester United; this article discusses mental health and suicide, which some readers may find distressing; if you have been affected by this story, support and guidance are available at sky.com/viewersupport Tuesday 17 November 2026 20:54, UK Image: Wayne Rooney has spoken candidly about his mental health struggles Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated suicide. The former England striker revealed that, despite enjoying success on the pitch, he was struggling with his mental health off it. Newly married and a father to eldest son Kai, Rooney would sometimes spend two days drinking at home. Speaking on the Life at the Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, he admitted that, at his lowest point, he had contemplated taking his own life. "I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with. Then I didn't want Kai seeing me like that, so that's why I'd hide away as well," Rooney said. "I got to a place where you're contemplating suicide. You just didn't want to be around anyone.
